newsitem.title: UK: UK windfall tax need not hit customers-Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK windfall tax need not hit customers-Brown.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, said a Labour government could take action to ensure its windfall levy on the profits of privatised utilities was not passed on to customers.
"I think the view of experts is that it will not and should not (be passed on)," he said in an interview in the London Evening Standard newspaper.
"I think we can take action to ensure that it should not affect them."
"I do not think many City people believe the utilities will be in a position to put up prices as a result of this. I think if you look at the legal powers available, it is not possible," Brown added.
On his plans for setting an inflation target, the shadow chancellor said: "I will be announcing my inflation target in the next few weeks."
Asked if three billion stg would be the least amount to be raised by the windfall tax, which Labour intends to fund a "welfare-to-work" programme, Brown replied:
"We may want to do more, but at a minimum the proposals will cost, over the life of a parliament, three billion pounds."
He said he was not in a position to announce what the levy would raise because this was a matter to be discussed with regulators when Labour was in government.
"But the programme will cost at a minimum three billion pounds and I am confident that we can meet that."
